text:
mia: Heads-up — just noticed a RoleBinding applied during a CI change that effectively let the deploy SA reach the GPU pool namespace and decrypt KMS-encrypted model keys. Not a confirmed compromise but it’s a least-priv issue we should lock down ASAP.

jasper: Ugh. Can you paste the RBAC YAML and the audit log snippet?

mia: Here’s the binding I found in the commit diff:

```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: gpu-deployer-binding
  namespace: infra
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: deployer-sa
    namespace: ci
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: gpu-accessor
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

mia: `gpu-accessor` was a ClusterRole created earlier to allow admin teams to patch GPU nodeLabeling. It contains `get/patch/exec` on several resources — looks broader than intended.

anita: Do we have an audit log showing decrypt requests from `deployer-sa`?

audit-bot: 2039001138 - k8s-audit - subject: system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer-sa - verb: create - resource: pods - namespace: gpu-pool
audit-bot: 2039001141 - kms-audit - principal: system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer-sa - action: Decrypt - key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/models/cryptoKey/model-enc-key - result: DENIED (policy mismatch)

mia: The KMS decrypt was DENIED in this case (thankfully). But the RBAC change would have allowed pod create in gpu-pool if combined with a container image that had the KMS client — so it was a near miss.

ryan: Good catch. Immediate actions: 1) remove binding, 2) rotate short-lived keys used by any CI SAs that had potential access, 3) add audit alert for any Decrypt attempts from non-prod namespaces. Thoughts?

jasper: +1. Also we should: add a validation gate to CI so ClusterRole vs RoleBinding mismatches get flagged (no cross-namespace ClusterRole binding from CI pipelines).

anita: Can we push a Gatekeeper constraint to block RoleBinding where roleRef.kind=="ClusterRole" and subject.namespace!=role.namespace? I can draft a constraint.

mia: That would help. For now I’ve opened a rollback PR to remove the binding and added a comment to rotate any long-lived tokens.

oncall-ops: Please also run `kubectl get events -n gpu-pool --since=1h` and check for suspicious pod creation commands. I’ll standby to revoke tokens if we see anything.

ryan: For permanent fixes we should: 1) convert gpu-accessor into a namespaced Role with narrowly scoped verbs, 2) enforce CI pipeline SA scoping (use projected/BoundServiceAccountToken), 3) add KMS allowlist by namespace via KMS IAM conditions (where supported).

mia: I’ll file an incident ticket with the timeline and link the rollback PR. Attaching checklist: remove binding, rotate any service credentials, add Gatekeeper constraint, add audit alert for KMS Decrypts from non-prod, update docs on Role vs ClusterRole usage in CI.

jasper: Thanks. Small follow-up — can someone grep audit logs for the last 7 days for any Decrypt ACCEPTs from `ci:` SAs? If any, escalate to forensics.

audit-bot: Running query: `kms.logs.filter("principal:system:serviceaccount:ci:")` -> 0 ACCEPT in last 7d, 3 DENIED.

mia: OK closing the loop here, will create follow-ups in the sec backlog and ping infra for the gatekeeper change.
